back: A long-term plan for using people, equipment, materials, money and technology to produce goods or services in line with the business's aims.
The ability of operations to change quickly and cheaply in volume, delivery time or specification as customers' needs change.
Volume = how much is made; delivery time = how fast orders are met; specification = what features the product has.
Changing the way goods or services are produced or delivered, by improving current processes or adopting new ways of working.
Human resources (numbers and skills), marketing (demand and promises made) and finance (cash for equipment and stock).
Can forecast demand, plan delivery routes, predict machine failure and check quality; costs money, needs data and skilled staff.
Temporary or part-time staff, overtime, subcontracting, leased equipment and spare capacity.
Spare capacity, multi-skilled workers and flexible equipment raise unit costs when they are not fully used.
Judge it against demand for variety or seasonal change, the cash available and the skills of the workforce.
